## Natural history notes

A small blue butterfly characterized by pale bluish upper wings in males, brownish-gray upper wings in females, and pale gray undersides marked with small dark spots and orange markings near the hindwing edge. In Florida, it is common in sunny open habitats such as fields, roadsides, gardens, pine flatwoods, coastal areas, and disturbed sites where low-growing legumes are present. Adults feed on nectar from small flowers, while the caterpillars feed on plants in the pea family, including partridge pea, beggarweeds, and other native or weedy legumes.
